newsitem.title: USA: Willis' "Fifth Element" first at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: Willis' "Fifth Element" first at U.S. box office.

text.p: "The Fifth Element," a French-made science fiction picture starring Bruce Willis, debuted in the top spot at the U.S. weekend box office according to studio estimates released on Sunday.

The movie earned about $17.2 million, placing it well in front of fellow newcomer "Fathers' Day," which pulled in $9 million. Last weekend's No. 1, "Breakdown," slipped to third with about $7.6 million in its second weekend.

"The Fifth Element," in which Willis plays a New York cab driver in the year 2259, was directed by France's Luc Besson, who also directed "La Femme Nikita." Besson conceived the story during his teen-aged years. It had its world premiere last week when it opened the Cannes Film Festival.

The film was produced by French company Gaumont SA and is distributed in the United States by Columbia Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp., which reportedly paid $25 million for the rights. It garnered the highest per-screen average in the top 10, with $6,880 from 2,500 screens.
"Fathers' Day," a comedy starring Robin Williams and Billy Crystal, averaged an unpromising $3,626 from 2,482 screens. The film was released by Time Warner Inc.'s Warner Bros.

"Breakdown," a thriller starring Kurt Russell and J.T. Walsh, has now earned $23.16 million after 10 days in release. Its weekend total fell 38 percent from its opening round, and it averaged $3,312 from 2,295 screens (an increase of 187 screens). The film is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc..

In fourth place, the Michael Myers spy spoof "Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery" recouped its $16 million production budget as its 10-day total rose to $19.5 million. The film earned $7.1 million this weekend, a drop of just 26 percent from last weekend when it opened in second. It averaged $3,246 from 2,187 screens. Time Warner's New Line Cinema released the picture.

"Volcano," the No. 1 movie two weeks ago, was fifth this weekend with $4.2 million, a slump of 52 percent from last weekend when it stood at third. Its 17-day total rose to $33.8 million, but the lava extravaganza reportedly cost News Corp.'s 20th Century Fox $100 million to make. This weekend, it averaged $1,584 from 2,652 screens.
